source.title: Learning Enhances Sensory and Multiple Non-sensory Representations in Primary Visual Cortex.

confidence_rationale: Included deliberately as the COUNTERWEIGHT entry. It shows learning improves the discriminability of task-relevant stimuli in V1 -- consistent with MECH-567 -- but it also shows V1 simultaneously acquires multiple NON-sensory signals, i.e. the encoder becomes less a clean sensory code and more a task-entangled one. That cuts against any simple 'just add the task target and the code gets better for everyone' reading, which matters because REE's z_world is a SHARED latent with many declared consumers.
failure_signatures: Enhanced discriminability is reported for the trained task; the paper does not test whether the reshaped V1 code is better or WORSE for an untrained downstream use, which is the shared-latent risk REE actually faces.
Non-sensory (choice, reward, locomotion) signals appearing in V1 mean task-shaping ENTANGLES the code; for a multi-consumer latent this is a cost, not only a benefit.
Mouse V1 in a head-fixed virtual-corridor discrimination task; the consumer is a licking report, far simpler than a policy over an action set.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Learning a visual discrimination task increases the discriminability of task-relevant stimuli in mouse V1 population activity, and concurrently V1 comes to represent multiple non-sensory variables including choice, reward and locomotion signals.
mapping.ree_translation: The first half supports MECH-567: task-relevant supervision reaching the encoder improves exactly the discriminations the consumer needs. The second half is the registered COST: task-shaping entangles the code with task variables. REE's z_world is explicitly a shared representation -- SD-106's own note lists SD-015, ARC-030, MECH-117, the EXQ-085h..o cluster, MECH-457 and ARC-065 as consumers -- so an unrestricted MECH-567 build risks improving one consumer at the expense of the others. This is the biological reason MECH-567 is registered as an AUXILIARY-HEAD claim (DreamerV3 shape) rather than as MuZero's consumer-only training, which would make z_world single-consumer by construction.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Neither half is measured against an UNTRAINED downstream use, so the shared-latent cost is inferred from the presence of non-sensory signals rather than demonstrated as a degradation. Recorded as a risk to instrument for, not as an established penalty.
mapping.source_context: Mouse V1 two-photon imaging across learning of a virtual-corridor visual discrimination task.

confidence_components.notes: Included for its counterweight value as much as its support. The shared-latent cost is the part REE most needs and is the part the paper evidences least directly.
